subject: Post-call: ACME long-context eval (next steps & recommended models)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: ACME long-context eval (next steps & recommended models)

Thanks for the call today — great discussion on the long-form summarization use case and the pain points you saw with truncation and topic drift. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

1) Scope: Evaluate on 250 real user sessions (500–8,000 token contexts) focusing on:
   - truncation behavior when context > model window
   - summarization fidelity for multi-topic conversations
   - hallucination/regression on entity preservation

2) Suggested baseline models for the eval:
   - redwood-13b-long (quantized) — strong latency/cost balance for 8k windows
   - redwood-34b-long — higher fidelity, better entity preservation for multi-topic summaries
   - llama-2-70b-chat (off-the-shelf) — to compare open baseline behavior on truncation

3) Artifacts we will deliver:
   - prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample + canonical prompts)
   - long_context_eval_report.pdf (benchmarks, examples, failure modes)
   - notebook with evaluation scripts and metrics (ROUGE, BEER, entity-F1, and custom truncation recall)

Next steps: I will run the 250-session eval and share the report by EOD Monday. Can you confirm the shared dataset and whether we should de-identify production emails before we run? Also please confirm if ACME prefers a follow-up technical review (30m) or a joint demo (45m) with your engineering team.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (JSONL, 48KB)]

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>

Date: 2027-08-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME long-context eval (next steps & recommended models)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 

- We can share 250 sessions; please run the eval on the raw text but strip any PII at your end. I'll share a S3 link with the dataset credentials by tomorrow.
- On model choices: our product lead is biased toward lower-cost inference; can you include a cheaper baseline (cpu-backed distil model or a 7B quantized) so we can understand cost/perf tradeoffs?
- Curious about your truncation metrics — how will you surface partial-context summaries (we saw cases where the model summarized only the tail and missed earlier decisions)?

We're open to a 30m technical review. Priya will coordinate schedules.

-Alex
Product Manager, ACME Corp
[Attachment: none]

Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME long-context eval (next steps & recommended models)

Alex — great, thanks for confirming. Quick answers inline and updated plan: 

- De-id: yes — please upload raw and we'll run a redaction pass (PII regex + manual spot checks). We'll mark any examples where redaction affects summary usefulness.

- Cheaper baseline: added redwood-7b-long-quant to the matrix (cheap, 4k window with longer context via sliding-window stitching). Will report tokens/sec and per-1k-token cost estimates so you can compare.

- Truncation metric: we will compute a truncation-recall metric that measures the fraction of ground-truth summary facts present when only the last N tokens are available. We'll include an analysis of which topics are lost as window shrinks and a visualization (heatmap) of where the model drops key entities. Example: when window truncated at 3,500 tokens the 13b model preserved 78% entity-F1 vs 94% when full context provided.

Deliverables timeline (updated):
- Wed 8/4: initial eval run on 50 sessions + quick sanity report
- Mon 8/9 EOD: full 250-session report (long_context_eval_report.pdf) + prompt_set_v1.jsonl + benchmark_results.csv

Ask: can Priya share preferred S3 path & a contact for credentials? If you want, I can include a short note about how to run the eval on your infra (Docker + evaluation notebook).

I'll kick off the first 50-session run now and will share preliminary failures.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: long_context_eval_report_draft.pdf (PDF, 520KB) — preliminary examples]
